metadata.title: USIR v5 Stage B-10: Gate 3a Scene-Level Denominator Redesign & Level 3b Scale Separation Report

gate_3a_official_decision.official_reason: Modern prose across registers (R1-R3) exhibits significant diachronic and genre-specific distributional shift relative to the pre-war Aozora Bunko baseline. While scene-level within-register scaling stabilizes metrics, uncentered modern prose continues to fail pre-war acceptance thresholds. Gate 3a remains officially SHIFT_QUANTIFIED_NOT_PASSED.

proposal_to_orion.summary: Formal proposal to Orion regarding future Gate 3a criteria update and transition to register-conditioned manifold modeling.
items: 1. Denominator Redesign: Replace work-level denominator sigma_work with scene-level denominator sigma_scene to match sample resolution (400-800 chars) and eliminate false outlier inflation (scale ratio 1.42x / variance 2.03x).
2. Finite-Sample LOO Adjustment: Account for the 1.2444x Student-t inflation at n_r=16 in thresholding; asymptotic chi2_0.95 naturally yields ~22-25% exceedance under finite-sample null.

3. Register-Conditioned Intake: Mandate Scheme 3 (Within-Register LOO Centering with Shrinkage Variance) for text ingestion, which achieves 100% elimination of between-register variance (eta^2 -> 0.000) while preserving internal distance geometry (rho=1.000).
4. Gate 3b Prerequisite: Maintain Gate 3b as GATE3B_FROZEN until automated register classification and conditioned standardization pipelines are validated.

gate_3b_official_decision.reason: Gate 3b remains strictly frozen pending Orion consensus and deployment of register-conditioned normalization pipeline.

task2_fixed_h1_h2_ratings.protocol: Two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test with Bonferroni correction (k=4)

fixed_ratings_summary.specificity_vs_other: Specificities vs other authors/styles remain statistically significant across all spaces after Bonferroni correction (k=4, two-sided p_bonf in [0.0129, 0.0420] < 0.05).
fixed_ratings_summary.specificity_vs_isotropic_random: Specificities vs isotropic random perturbations are nominal p < 0.05 at best and do NOT survive two-sided Bonferroni correction (k=4); in H2 5D continuous core (4pole_cont_plus_hw25), vs-random effect completely disappears (p_two = 0.4060, bonferroni_p_two = 1.0000).
prohibited_claims_guard: Do NOT claim 'approach toward target exceeding random' on the macro side.
Do NOT claim 'discrete poles carried a spurious signal' for the 5D cos drop.

covariance_rank_deficiency_diagnostic.explanation: With n_r=16 samples per register, LOO sample covariance has degrees of freedom nu=14. Since dimension d=24 > nu=14, the sample covariance matrix is mathematically rank-deficient. Diagonal shrinkage (0.15) inverts near-nullspace noise, producing 81.25% false outliers on the R4 self-control cohort. This proves why univariate scene-level variance is necessary.

With n_r=16 samples per register, LOO sample covariance has degrees of freedom nu=14. Since dimension d=31 > nu=14, the sample covariance matrix is mathematically rank-deficient. Diagonal shrinkage (0.15) inverts near-nullspace noise, producing 93.75% false outliers on the R4 self-control cohort. This proves why univariate scene-level variance is necessary.

1_scale_ratio_scene_vs_work_23_active_di.explanation: Scene-level variance sigma_scene^2 is on average 2.2645x larger than work-level variance sigma_work^2 (mean scale ratio 1.4233x, (mean)^2 = 2.0258x) due to short-scene sample variance vs full-book averaging. B-9 evaluated scenes against work-level denominators, creating an artificial 81.25% (31D) / 62.50% (24D) outlier rate on R4. Using sigma_scene resolves this scale mismatch.

2_finite_sample_loo_student_t_inflation.explanation: Under LOO at n_r=16 (m=15, nu=14), standardized distance squares follow a scaled Student-t distribution with E[D^2] inflated by 1.2444x. Consequently, the nominal 5% asymptotic chi2_0.95 threshold is exceeded by 22.29% (independent) to 24.51% (R4-correlated) of true null samples. This proves that the observed R4 exceedance rate (~25-31%) is an expected mathematical property of finite-sample LOO, not abnormal register shift.

4_single_nonzero_loo_variance_collapse_3.explanation: When only a single sample in a cohort has a non-zero value on a sparse particle dimension (v2_final_ぬ in R4_16), omitting it produces zero LOO variance, hitting the 1e-6 floor and exploding distance to 52.79. Shrinkage LOO (18.38) and in-sample variance (5.32) prevent this collapse.

reference_only_scheme_2.disclaimer: 本値は自己レジスター平均を減算した差分を他分布（青空文庫アトラス）の分散で除算した同義反復的補正（self-register mean subtraction divided by another distribution's sigma）であり、独立した収束証拠とはみなさない参考値である。

two_scale_lens_formal_rating.description: 平均 cos_spec ≈ +0.11〜+0.14、対他者有意、対ランダム名目 p<0.05 で支持。離散・死滅次元を除去した有効連続サブセット（Micro: ortho24_cont+kasane8_active 32D, Macro: 4pole_cont+HW-25 5D）においても、ミクロ推敲における表層直交・重ねリズム特異性（vs 他者 Bonferroni p=0.0210, vs ランダム Bonferroni p=0.0476）およびマクロ改稿におけるスタイル特異性（vs 他者 Bonferroni p=0.0065）が頑健に成立。

sample_size_stability.n_32_to_n_64_comparison: Doubling sample size from 32 to 64 narrows 95% bootstrap CIs and eliminates single-sample variance collapse in larger cohorts.

core_scientific_findings: 1. Both Baseline A (in-benchmark R4 diagonal) and Baseline B (Aozora 106-works Atlas) confirm severe modern register shift (Baseline A R2=75-87.5%, R3=100% 3-sigma; Baseline B overall modern ~95.8% 3-sigma).
2. Scheme 1 (Continuous Core 24D) removes sparse dimensions but cannot eliminate register/era shift by itself.

3. Scheme 2 (LOO Era Shift Alignment) cleanly aligns R1 colloquial fiction into the literary manifold (3-sigma outlier rate drops to 0.0% on both Baseline A and Baseline B 24D in n=64, and chi2_0.95 drops to 0.0% on Baseline A).
4. Scheme 2 on pooled modern prose (R1-R3) fails to resolve R2/R3 outliers, demonstrating genre/register drift is orthogonal to chronological era drift.

5. Scheme 3 (Within-Register LOO Centering) achieves 100% elimination of between-register variance (eta^2 -> 0.000) and rho=1.000 distance fidelity, with 0.0% 3-sigma / 4.17% chi2 modern outlier rate under shrinkage LOO variance (while exposing single-nonzero LOO variance collapse on unregularized small cohorts).
